guide.title: Beethoven: String Quartet Op. 18 No. 5 – IV. Allegro
guide.overview: This is a quick movement in A major. It has two big parts, and the first part is repeated. A light, bouncing main tune opens the movement and comes back several times. Listen for the tune, for sudden drops from loud to very soft, and for the long very loud stretch in the middle of Part 2. The final return of the tune leads to a playful, quiet close.

listening_points.headline: The main tune appears, soft and light
listening_points.text: The viola starts alone, quietly [m. 0]. Then Violin 1 plays the main tune over a gentle accompaniment [m. 1-3]. Everything is soft here. The key is A major, the home key.

listening_points.headline: Violin 1 leads in a calm A major
listening_points.text: Violin 1 probably carries the tune for most of this stretch. The others mostly accompany. The music stays soft and settled in the home key.

listening_points.headline: A brighter key: E major
listening_points.text: The music moves to E major. This is a new key, and it sounds like a fresh area. The violins pass little phrases back and forth. Leadership is shared here, so who has the tune is unclear.

listening_points.headline: Loud, then a sudden whisper
listening_points.text: A crescendo (getting louder) leads to two loud bars [m. 34-35]. Then the music drops to very soft at [m. 36]. The soft phrases sound hushed. Another crescendo starts at [m. 40].

listening_points.headline: Sharp accents, a loud burst, then a hush
listening_points.text: Sharp accents (sf, a sudden strong note) poke through the soft playing [m. 51-64]. Then comes a loud moment [m. 65]. Violin 1 is alone at [m. 66]. After that the music falls to very soft [m. 67].

listening_points.headline: Repeating patterns wind down Part 1
listening_points.text: Violin 1 plays a four-bar pattern twice [m. 71-78]. Then the parts take turns in small groups. The viola and Violin 2 each get a moment [m. 83-85]. At [m. 92] the music returns to A major.

listening_points.headline: Part 2 begins in a darker key
listening_points.text: The music slips into F# minor, a darker key. The viola plays alone as Part 2 starts [m. 94]. Then the music stays loud [m. 95-98], first with three parts and then with the tune over accompaniment. Sharp accents mark the end of this phrase.

listening_points.headline: The tune returns in D major
listening_points.text: A short stop in C# minor leads to a hush [m. 99-100]. Then Violin 1 plays the main tune in D major, loud [m. 103-104]. The tune has the same shape but sits higher. It is easy to spot.

listening_points.headline: Stormy minor keys and fortissimo
listening_points.text: The mood turns stormy in D minor and then C minor. The volume jumps to ff, very loud, at [m. 114]. The harmony shifts quickly, so the music feels unsettled.

listening_points.headline: C major, very loud throughout
listening_points.text: The music brightens to C major but stays very loud. Accents hit again and again. The analysis marks [m. 128] as the busiest point.

listening_points.headline: Sudden calm, then very soft
listening_points.text: After the peak the music drops to soft [m. 132]. Then it gets even softer, to pp [m. 135]. The parts weave quiet lines. Around [m. 143] the key darkens to A minor.

listening_points.headline: Back to A major, growing toward the return
listening_points.text: A major comes back at [m. 147], still very soft. A crescendo starts at [m. 148]. The music then settles to soft [m. 166]. The viola plays alone at [m. 167] and leads into the tune.

listening_points.headline: The opening tune comes home
listening_points.text: Violin 1 plays the main tune again in A major, soft [m. 168-170]. It is just as at the start. This is a clear return.

listening_points.headline: Loud chord, then hush, as before
listening_points.text: A crescendo leads to two loud bars [m. 205-206]. Then the music drops to very soft [m. 207]. You heard this loud-to-soft drop in Part 1, but now it stays in A major.

listening_points.headline: Final return of the tune, loud
listening_points.text: Violin 1 plays the main tune one last time, now loud [m. 264-266]. Accents push it forward. Then it goes soft again for steady phrases [m. 269].

listening_points.headline: Loud accents, a soft stretch, and a quiet final chord
listening_points.text: Loud accents return briefly [m. 281-284], then the music hushes again [m. 285]. Violin 1 leads a soft closing stretch [m. 289-296]. The cello has a loud last statement [m. 297-298]. A short, soft chord ends it [m. 299].

glossary.explanation: The home note and scale that the music is built around. Major sounds brighter. Minor sounds darker.
A move from one key to another.
A sudden, sharp accent on a note or chord.
Loudness markings: p is soft, pp is very soft, f is loud, ff is very loud.
The tune that Violin 1 plays at the start. It comes back several times.
How the parts fit together, for example one tune with accompaniment, or several equal lines.
All parts move together with the same rhythm, like a hymn.
